record.original_question: If Γ is a normal conilpotent subgroup of a uniform lattice in SL(2,R), is the Haar measure nonsquashable, meaning that the centralizer of the horocycle flow does not contain an invertible nonsingular transformation that fails to preserve the measure?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $G=\mathrm{SL}(2,\mathbb{R})$ and let $\{u_t\}_{t\in\mathbb{R}}$ denote the one-parameter subgroup
$$u_t=\begin{pmatrix}1 & t\\ 0 & 1\end{pmatrix},$$
acting on quotients $\Gamma\backslash G$ by right translation; this action is the horocycle flow.

Let $\Lambda<G$ be a uniform (cocompact) lattice. A subgroup $\Gamma\trianglelefteq\Lambda$ is called conilpotent if the quotient $\Lambda/\Gamma$ is a nilpotent group. Assume that $\Gamma$ is a normal conilpotent subgroup of $\Lambda$; then $\Gamma$ is a discrete subgroup of $G$ and the right $u_t$-action on $\Gamma\backslash G$ preserves the Haar measure $\mu$ (the $G$-invariant Radon measure inherited from Haar measure on $G$).

For a $u_t$-invariant Radon measure $\mu$ on a standard Borel space carrying the horocycle flow, the centralizer of $u_t$ is the group of invertible nonsingular (Borel) transformations that commute with $u_t$ modulo $\mu$-null sets. The measure $\mu$ is called squashable if its centralizer contains an invertible nonsingular transformation $T$ such that $T_*\mu$ is not a scalar multiple of $\mu$; otherwise $\mu$ is called nonsquashable.

Question: Is the Haar measure on $\Gamma\backslash G$ nonsquashable under the horocycle flow?
artifact.status_search_result: Searches surface the work of Babillot–Ledrappier and Sarig classifying ergodic invariant Radon measures for horocycle flows on regular covers of compact hyperbolic surfaces, where squashability is studied for abelian covers (yielding nonsquashability of one distinguished measure). However, no source could be located that resolves the specific question of nonsquashability of the Haar measure for arbitrary normal conilpotent subgroups (i.e., general nilpotent covers) of uniform lattices in SL(2,R). Status appears to remain open or unresolved in the available literature.

status_evidence.title: Invariant Radon measures for horocycle flows on Abelian covers
status_evidence.snippet: Classification of ergodic invariant Radon measures for the horocycle flow on Z^d-covers of compact hyperbolic surfaces, proving Babillot–Ledrappier conjecture.
status_evidence.claim: The abelian-cover case is handled by Sarig; the nilpotent-cover generalization is the natural next step.

status_evidence.title: Horocycle flows on surfaces with infinite genus (Sarig notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of squashable measures and classification results for horocycle flows on infinite-genus surfaces, with attention to polynomial growth/nilpotent quotients.
status_evidence.claim: Squashability framework is developed for these covers, but the general normal conilpotent case is not stated as resolved.
